description: Me gusta la idea de saber que más hay en el espacio
summary:
"Remembering the Space" is an animation born from the "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" challenge, where we tell the story of objects that were lost and left behind in space since their arrival there. In our animation, we follow the journey of iconic hardware like the lunar module, the Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG), and the Spirit and Opportunity rovers on Mars, showing what happened to them after their missions ended.
To develop this project, we researched real NASA history and mission details to make sure these objects were represented accurately in our story. We wanted to move beyond simple technical facts and show the real journey these machines went through in space.
For us, this project is really important because we want to reach children and young people. Often, older space missions get forgotten as new technology appears, even though they made everything possible today. Through this animation, our main goal is to connect with a younger audience, spark their curiosity about what is out there, and inspire them to enter the world of science and space exploration.
details: This is an animated video aimed at kids and teenagers interested in science, with the goal of inspiring them and sparking a lifelong passion for knowledge. The animation and editing were entirely created by young people using Ibispaint and CapCut, designed to be dynamic and engaging for young audiences. Creativity, education, and inspiration were key factors in bringing this project to life.
